rows.title: With Denver Summit FC, Rob Cohen is betting on Colorado falling in love with pro women’s sports
rows.standfirst: The chairman and CEO of IMA Financial has spent decades advocating for Denver as the founder of the city’s sports commission. Now he has a team of his own.

rows.title: A once-blighted riverfront property is helping Grand Junction spur economic activity — just not exactly as envisioned
rows.standfirst: The $30 million revival of Las Colonias development along a stretch of Colorado River is starting to pay off despite competition from nearby Montrose

rows.title: $10 stadium hot dog in Colorado lives on as effort to prevent high “captive audience” pricing meets demise
rows.standfirst: House Bill 1012 was rejected Tuesday during its first hearing at the Colorado Capitol. It faced big opposition from the business community.

rows.title: Do you use cash advance apps like MoneyLion, EarnIn or Brigit? We want to hear from you.
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun wants to talk to you about your experience using apps to access money before your paycheck arrives

rows.title: How state investment is helping the North Fork Valley transition from coal to culture
rows.standfirst: The state Office of Just Transition has awarded $9M in grants to replace jobs and tax dollars if and when coal is gone, including for small businesses in Paonia

rows.title: American outdoor recreation economy tops $1.3 trillion, with Colorado again in the top 10 states
rows.standfirst: The latest Bureau of Economic Analysis numbers show the growing outdoor recreation sector as a critical economic engine for rural America. Colorado’s outdoor economy again ranks in the top 10 in the nation.

rows.title: What’s Working: Imposter-scam complaints decline in Colorado, but consumer complaints hit record
rows.standfirst: Trying to combat spammy texts? Forward them to 7726. Plus: Just 23 complaints logged after junk fees law takes effect, CSU Fort Collins teams with Pueblo on nursing, more!

rows.title: Colorado wants help picking a name for Front Range passenger train ahead of November vote to fund route
rows.standfirst: The district wants to settle on a name before deciding whether to put a measure on the ballot that would increase sales taxes along the Front Range

rows.title: Energy Secretary Chris Wright, during Colorado stop, warns that high gas prices could last weeks
rows.standfirst: Wright said the US will insure oil tankers traveling through the Strait of Hormuz and will even use the military to escort ships

rows.title: Nearly 3,800 JBS unionized meatpackers in Greeley plan to strike March 16
rows.standfirst: They’ve been working on an expired contract for eight months. JBS officials accused the union of not sharing the company’s latest offer with workers.

rows.title: Ambulance services would get funding boost while saving Colorado millions under new bill
rows.standfirst: Sometimes it’s cheaper to treat a patient at home, but for EMS to be paid for the service, the person must be taken to the hospital

rows.title: Xcel claims it can’t close the electricity supply gap yet, floats the idea of keeping its coal plants running until 2030
rows.standfirst: The plants in Pueblo and Hayden were slated to phase out between 2025 and 2030. Now the company has proposed running all their units for four more years.

rows.title: It’s up to Colorado to shield consumers from the price shock of Xcel Energy’s data center-related building boom
rows.standfirst: Colorado utilities regulators have a tall order: cut pollution, promote electrification and economic development while slowing rise of electric bills

rows.title: Colorado effort to end credit card swipe fees on sales taxes is splitting businesses
rows.standfirst: Companies paid $2.1 billion in swipe fees in 2024 for the right to accept credit cards. They’re fighting to get back $200 million charged on sales tax. Banks and other businesses say it’s not that simple.

rows.title: What’s Working: Denver leads US for apartment concessions as landlords aim to fill oversupply
rows.standfirst: A Golden Triangle tenant won a free year of rent. Plus: 3 Colorado cities land on top hot spots for Gen Z renters, taxes on sports betting hit monthly high, a tobacco-based job fair and more!

rows.title: Thousands of JBS workers go on strike at meatpacking facility in Greeley
rows.standfirst: Meatpackers have not struck in more than 40 years. The Greeley walkout happened after 8 months of talks about pay and working conditions failed.

rows.title: Grand Junction’s primary homeless shelter just closed. WEShelter can fill only some of the void.
rows.standfirst: While WEShelter and other small Grand Junction shelters provide vital services, they are unable to fill the void left by the closure of the city’s main shelter.

rows.title: Some workers striking at the JBS meatpacking facility say they were put in danger on the job
rows.standfirst: But the meatpacking giant in Greeley says others are not joining the picket line and coming to work instead, for “stability” and to “support their families”

rows.title: AI policy group makes recommendations on tweaks to Colorado’s first-of-its-kind artificial intelligence law
rows.standfirst: The working group recommendations still need to be ironed out at the state Capitol in a bill and would need to clear the legislature this session

rows.title: Chevron’s $1.5M fine for Weld County blowout will finance improvements to monitoring programs
rows.standfirst: Colorado energy commissioners OK penalty for largest well blowout in a decade, but some environmental groups say it doesn’t cover damages to the community

rows.title: Colorado’s state budget shortfall grows to more than $1.5 billion, forcing legislature to make much deeper cuts
rows.standfirst: The legislature’s Joint Budget Committee has already been slashing spending for weeks as it works to draft the state’s 2026-27 fiscal year budget. That includes cuts to Medicaid, which is the primary driver of the state’s budget shortfall.

rows.title: Do homes in Aspen sell for more than $12M on average?
rows.standfirst: Yes. The average sale price of a single-family home in Aspen in 2025 was $17.3 million, an Aspen Board of Realtors report shows.

rows.title: Colorado is losing 1 affordable housing unit for every 2 it builds. But the state keeps rejecting efforts to stop the bleeding.
rows.standfirst: Gov. Jared Polis and state housing officials have prioritized new construction over preserving existing affordable rental housing.

rows.title: Google taps Boulder physicist to head up new quantum-computing team in Colorado
rows.standfirst: It’s the company’s first toehold into the local quantum ecosystem. Adam Kaufman, known for his work in neutral atoms, is also key to Google’s big expansion to develop its first quantum computer faster

rows.title: Colorado lawmakers are pursuing state’s first guardrails on online betting since sports wagers began
rows.standfirst: The push has opened a fight over addiction, financial harm and whether the state has grown too dependent on gambling revenue

rows.title: Tegna-Nexstar megamerger drama has national implications, but seismic impact on Denver news
rows.standfirst: Combining newsleaders 9News and Fox31 already has triggered a lawsuit and concerned experts — and not just because of what might happen to Kyle Clark

rows.title: Colorado governor signs bill letting schools, universities bypass some zoning rules to build housing
rows.standfirst: The bill requires local governments with populations over 2,000 people to, starting in 2028, allow qualifying organizations to build residential units on their land whether or not the land is zoned for residential construction

rows.title: Colorado data center bills split environmental, labor groups
rows.standfirst: At the core of the dispute is a legislative proposal to rein in the energy-hungry facilities powering the artificial intelligence boom

rows.title: Comanche 3 repairs delayed again, raising fears of summer power shortages that demand customer cutbacks
rows.standfirst: Xcel Energy has until April 15 to present a plan for dealing with the projected electricity shortfall during the hottest days of summer

rows.title: A waitlist for 24/7 care for Colorado adults with disabilities is 7 years long. State Medicaid cuts could double it.
rows.standfirst: After years of trying to clear the waitlist for the adult developmental disabilities waiver, this year’s budget crisis could double it

rows.title: Workers’ strike at Greeley JBS meatpacking plant will continue for a 3rd week
rows.standfirst: Industry experts said it’s too early to know if the strike that began March 16 at the Swift Beef Co. plant will impact beef prices for shoppers

rows.title: Nexstar-Tegna megamerger blocked by ruling in antitrust case filed by DirecTV
rows.standfirst: Case filed against the owners of Fox31 and 9News in Denver by 8 states, including Colorado, is still pending

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s largest hemp grower fears big staff layoffs under new federal rules
rows.standfirst: Plus: 859 wage-theft cases, more Denver office-to-apartments conversions, JBS worker strike to hit week three, carbon credits, more!

rows.title: How tiny Kit Carson County has grown into a green energy giant
rows.standfirst: A renewable energy building boom is changing the landscape — and the economic fortunes — on Colorado’s Eastern Plains

rows.title: Colorado importers hope for some of the $166 billion in tariff refunds as portal plans mid-April opening
rows.standfirst: Companies need to take action once the portal opens to process payment claims following Supreme Court decision that Trump administration tariffs were illegal

rows.title: Lawmakers reject lower overtime pay threshold for Colorado farmworkers, instead advance effort to increase it
rows.standfirst: Under the current law, which took full effect in 2025, overtime for farmworkers kicks in after either 56 or 48 hours of work in a week, depending on the type of farm work

rows.title: Shelley Read’s bestselling novel, “Go as a River,” is bringing a flood of literary tourism to this dry corner of Colorado
rows.standfirst: Visitors to the Gunnison Valley are looking for the lost town of Iola, imagined cabins and peach orchards, and asking how best to run into the author in downtown Crested Butte

rows.title: Colorado SunFest 2026 panel: Housing – Any relief in the high country?
rows.standfirst: Kimball Crangle and Tim Wohlgenant will speak about the high cost of housing in the high country during Colorado SunFest 2026.
